newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS REACHES SEMIFINALS, BECKER TO MEET KRAJICEK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS REACHES SEMIFINALS, BECKER TO MEET KRAJICEK.

text.p: Pete Sampras put an emotional defeat by Boris Becker to the back of his mind on Friday and strode into a semifinal showdown with big-serving Goran Ivanisevic at the ATP world championship.

The American world number one, who suffered his second defeat by Becker within a month on Thursday, knocked Russia's French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov out of the event with a clinical 6-4 6-4 victory in 75 minutes.
Sampras will now take on Ivanisevic, whom he has beaten in two of their three clashes this year, the last in the semifinals of the U.S. Open when the American won in four sets.

In Saturday's second semifinal Boris Becker, who lost a meaningless final group match against Swedish replacement Thomas Enqvist 6-3 7-6 on his 29th birthday on Friday, will meet Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek.
The Dutchman has to work hard to make sure of his place in the last four with a 7-6 6-7 6-3 victory over Austrian Thomas Muster in the final match of the round-robin stage.

Sampras knows he might have another chance to take on Becker if he makes Sunday's final. But the U.S. Open champion is taking nothing for granted with Ivanisevic's powerful serve likely to be cause problems on the fast Hanover court.
"I have got my hands full against Goran," he said. "Tomorrow will be another roller-coaster ride. If he serves and returns well he could blow me off court."

Becker has not played Krajicek for more than a year. The last time they met was at the 1995 Paris indoor event when the German won. The three-times Wimbledon champion has a major advantage in front of his fanatical home fans, however.

They presented him with a birthday cake after Friday's match against Enqvist which he described as an "exhibition." On Saturday the 15,000 crowd will roar Becker's every move and the German will thrive on the incessant chanting, clapping and stamping of feet.
"He has got a lead," Sampras said. "The conditions suit his game. The crowd. He is getting out of the blocks a bit sooner than anyone else."
Sampras showed why he is the best player in the world with his victory over Kafelnikov. It was effective,. if not perfect.

The American admitted his 7-6 7-6 defeat by Becker on Thursday had been tough to swallow. The fact that the 25- year-old American can bounce back the next day and beat a player who hits the ball as hard as Kafelnikov does proves his class.
"I would have prefered a day off. It was not easy. It was mentally draining," he said. "But today was a new day. I woke up and tried to put what happened against Becker behind me."

Being successful on the busy Tour is as much about consistency as class. Sampras sets himself apart from the rest because he has the ability to lift himself out of trouble when he is not feeling or playing at his best.
It is a quality that is missing from the make-up of some of his rivals such as his compatriot Andre Agassi or indeed Ivanisevic, who can be brilliant on some days, spineless on others.
